name: Barr's Cranefly Larva
imitates: A cranefly larva, a fat segmented grub that trout eat year-round in tailwaters and spring creeks; fished deep near the bottom.
recipe: Coarse synthetic dubbing (Arizona, Emergence or Sow Scud)

steps.text: Wrap about thirty turns of large lead wire along the shank, stopping a couple of eye lengths behind the eye and just short of the bend.
Start the thread in front of the lead, build a slight taper up to it, then wrap back over the lead to the bend as a smooth base and return to the front.
Clump the tip of a marabou feather about a hook gap long and tie it in at the bend with the tip extending off the back.
Fold the rest of the marabou forward over the shank and wrap the thread forward over it to behind the eye, forming a smooth underbody.
Clip the marabou butts at the eye, then tie a length of tippet on the far side of the hook for the rib and wrap back over it to the bend.
Let the tippet hang at the rear, return the thread to mid-shank, and cut a strip of Thinskin slightly narrower than the hook gap, peeling off its paper backing.
Lay the Thinskin on top of the shank at mid-point, fold it around the hook, and tie it down firmly at the front end.
Pull back on the Thinskin to stretch it slightly and wrap back over it to the base of the tail so it cups the shank.
Dub the thread heavily and build a tapered body from the bend, doing the rear half first with one strand and the front half with another.
Add more dubbing to finish an elongated football-shaped body, fattest in the middle and tapered at both ends.
Pull the Thinskin forward over the body and tie it down behind the eye, letting it buckle over the dubbing. Do not trim it yet.
Rib forward with the tippet in about a dozen evenly spaced turns, pulling tight so it sinks in and makes distinct segments.
Tie off and trim the ribbing and Thinskin at the eye, build a tapered thread head, whip finish, trim the dubbing underneath a bit, and add head cement. The finished fly.
